card: This pull request refactors CI environment scripts across 25 platforms to assemble the BITCOIN_CONFIG string using printf instead of multi-line strings. This allows CI maintainers to place explanatory comments adjacent to the specific configuration flags without triggering ShellCheck warnings. It also updates FUZZ_TESTS_CONFIG parsing in the test script to use an eval-constructed array. The author notes this is an internal CI documentation and style cleanup with no behavioral impact.
changed_since_previous: Added a commit converting `FUZZ_TESTS_CONFIG` into an argv array via `eval` in `03_test_script.sh` instead of expanding it unquoted with an SC2086 lint suppression.
evidence: Author states: "This is a CI doc-style-cleanup. BITCOIN_CONFIG is a single manually-formatted large string. This is fine, but shellcheck doesn't like when trailing comments are added: SC2155 -- Declare and assign separately."
problem: Multi-line string assignments in shell scripts prevent placing comments directly next to the configuration options they document without breaking syntax or triggering ShellCheck warnings (such as SC2155). Unquoted expansion of config strings like `FUZZ_TESTS_CONFIG` also required disabling ShellCheck lint rules (SC2086).

risk.why: A syntax or quoting bug in CI shell scripts could cause CI test environments to misconfigure or fail.

scope_notes: A mechanical formatting cleanup across 25 CI environment setup files plus one test runner script.
summary: Refactors CI environment scripts to construct `BITCOIN_CONFIG` via `printf -v` instead of a multi-line quoted string, placing explanatory comments directly adjacent to the relevant build options. In addition, converts `FUZZ_TESTS_CONFIG` into an array via `eval` in `03_test_script.sh` to avoid unquoted word-splitting.
